question: Does the criterion-level abstention mechanism fire MORE out-of-domain (BCN) than in-domain (Derm7pt test)? A spike => the checklist path fails safe (abstains rather than guesses) under the same shift that G8 showed degrades its accuracy.

g8_link.g8_finding: Derm7pt-trained criteria path is out-of-domain on BCN: melanoma AUROC 0.68, catches only 2 melanomas the in-domain BCN classifier misses (a real boundary).

honest_comparison_note: ORIGINAL 512-d dermlip heads only. criterion_abstention_v1.json was fit on those heads; its cutoffs are calibrated to their margin scale. The promoted 526-d (dermlip_tta+metadata14) heads CANNOT be built for BCN (no cached TTA view, no Derm7pt-style metadata for BCN), so a promoted-head cross-domain comparison is not computable -- reported as such, not faked. Both datasets share the plain unit-norm DermLIP_ViT-B-16 512-d view, so this comparison has no normalisation confound.

promoted_head_version.reason: BCN carries only the plain dermlip view; dermlip_tta is not cached for BCN and Derm7pt metadata14 (sex/location/elevation) has no BCN analogue in the frozen feature set. The 526-d promoted vector cannot be assembled for BCN, so the v1 policy cannot be applied to promoted heads out-of-domain. In-domain, run_cohort itself already declines to gate the promoted balanced heads with the v1 cutoffs (they are the wrong scale) -- see run_cohort.py _head_values_and_margins.

boundaries.heads: original dermlip 512-d, LogisticRegression C=10 unbalanced, fit on Derm7pt train
boundaries.abstention_policy: criterion_abstention_v1 (margin cutoffs, fit on Derm7pt train OOF)

class_distribution.note: Different class mixes are themselves part of the shift; a NEV-only matched control is reported separately.

verdict: NO SPIKE -- and the mechanism cuts the WRONG way (a substantive negative, not just a null). Out-of-domain the abstention rate is slightly LOWER (headroom-criteria read-rate delta -0.0386, undecidable-verdict delta -0.0680), because the frozen criterion heads become on average MORE confident on BCN inputs, not less: mean head margin WIDENS by +0.0534 across the criteria that can abstain. A margin-based abstention policy fit in-domain therefore does NOT fail safe under centre shift -- the probe can be confidently wrong on out-of-domain lesions and the in-domain-calibrated cutoffs will not catch it, so the criteria path commits rather than abstains exactly where G8 showed its accuracy has collapsed. The honest claim is narrow: criterion-margin abstention is an IN-DISTRIBUTION selective-prediction tool (it separates confident from unsure readings within a centre), NOT an out-of-domain guard. A real cross-centre safety gate needs an explicit distribution-shift / OOD detector on the feature side, which this margin policy is not. The NEV-only matched-class control shows the same direction, so this is not a class-mix artefact. Pooling robustness: BCN at IMAGE level (single image, no lesion pooling; n=9846) shows the SAME direction (headroom read-rate delta -0.0258, undecidable delta -0.0368, mean-margin delta +0.0380), so the no-spike finding is not an artefact of mean-pooling toward lesion centroids.
